description: This topic covers water as a compound and its physical properties, water as a solvent, hard and soft water with the causes and removal of hardness, tests and treatment of water for domestic use, and the properties, decomposition and uses of hydrogen peroxide.

mcq.questionText: What is the correct chemical formula of water?
mcq.explanation: A water molecule is made of two hydrogen atoms joined to one oxygen atom, giving the formula H2O.

mcq.questionText: Pure water boils at which temperature at normal atmospheric pressure?
mcq.explanation: At standard atmospheric pressure pure water boils at 100 degrees Celsius and freezes at 0 degrees Celsius.

mcq.questionText: Why is water often described as a 'universal solvent'?

options.text: It dissolves a very wide range of substances
It can dissolve absolutely every substance
It is found everywhere on Earth
It is used in all universities

mcq.explanation: Water dissolves a larger variety of substances than most other liquids, but not all substances, so it is called the universal solvent.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is the main cause of hardness in water?
mcq.explanation: Hardness is caused mainly by dissolved calcium and magnesium salts in the water.

mcq.questionText: Which type of water hardness can be removed simply by boiling?
mcq.explanation: Temporary hardness, caused by hydrogencarbonates, is removed by boiling because the hydrogencarbonates decompose into insoluble carbonates.

mcq.questionText: Which chemical test is used to confirm that a liquid is water?

options.text: It turns anhydrous copper(II) sulphate from white to blue

mcq.explanation: Water turns white anhydrous copper(II) sulphate blue, and also turns blue cobalt chloride paper pink, confirming its presence.

mcq.questionText: Which substance is added to water during domestic treatment to kill harmful germs?
mcq.explanation: Chlorine is added during water treatment because it kills bacteria and other disease-causing micro-organisms.

mcq.questionText: During water treatment, what is the purpose of adding alum?

options.text: To make small suspended particles clump together and settle

mcq.explanation: Alum acts as a coagulant, causing tiny suspended particles to join into larger clumps that settle out during sedimentation.

mcq.questionText: What is the chemical formula of hydrogen peroxide?
mcq.explanation: Hydrogen peroxide has the formula H2O2, containing one more oxygen atom per molecule than water.

mcq.questionText: When hydrogen peroxide decomposes, which two products are formed?
mcq.explanation: Hydrogen peroxide decomposes into water and oxygen gas: 2H2O2 gives 2H2O plus O2.

mcq.questionText: Which substance is commonly used as a catalyst to speed up the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide?
mcq.explanation: Manganese(IV) oxide acts as a catalyst, greatly speeding up the breakdown of hydrogen peroxide without being used up.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a common domestic use of hydrogen peroxide?

options.text: As a mild antiseptic to clean wounds

mcq.explanation: Dilute hydrogen peroxide is used as an antiseptic to clean wounds and is also used as a bleaching agent for hair and fabrics.

mcq.questionText: A sample of water forms little lather with soap but lathers easily after boiling. What does this indicate?

options.text: The water has permanent hardness only

mcq.explanation: Because boiling removes the hardness and restores lathering, the hardness must be temporary hardness.

mcq.questionText: Why is hydrogen peroxide usually stored in dark, opaque bottles?

options.text: Because light speeds up its decomposition

mcq.explanation: Light helps to break down hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen, so dark bottles slow this unwanted decomposition.

mcq.questionText: Which process removes dissolved salts and germs to produce the purest possible water in the laboratory?
mcq.explanation: Distillation boils the water and condenses the steam, leaving dissolved salts and most impurities behind to give very pure water.

fib.questionText: A water molecule is made up of two hydrogen atoms and one _____ atom.
fib.explanation: Water has the formula H2O, so each molecule contains one oxygen atom.

fib.questionText: The chemical formula of water is _____.
fib.explanation: Two hydrogen atoms combine with one oxygen atom to form H2O.

fib.questionText: Water that lathers easily with soap is described as _____ water.
fib.explanation: Soft water contains few calcium and magnesium ions, so it lathers readily.

fib.questionText: Hardness of water that cannot be removed by boiling is called _____ hardness.
fib.explanation: Permanent hardness is caused by dissolved sulphates and chlorides of calcium and magnesium and is removed by adding washing soda.

fib.questionText: The chemical added to water during treatment to kill germs is _____.
fib.explanation: Chlorine disinfects water by killing harmful bacteria and other micro-organisms.

fib.questionText: Anhydrous copper(II) sulphate changes from white to _____ in the presence of water.
fib.explanation: This colour change is a chemical test confirming the presence of water.

fib.questionText: The chemical formula of hydrogen peroxide is _____.
fib.explanation: Hydrogen peroxide has two hydrogen and two oxygen atoms per molecule.

fib.questionText: When hydrogen peroxide decomposes it produces water and _____ gas.
fib.explanation: The decomposition equation is 2H2O2 gives 2H2O plus O2.

fib.questionText: The catalyst commonly used to speed up the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide is manganese(IV) _____.
fib.explanation: Manganese(IV) oxide speeds up the reaction without being used up.

fib.questionText: Removing solid floating particles from water by passing it through sand or cloth is called _____.
fib.explanation: Filtration traps suspended solids and lets the clearer water pass through.

tf.questionText: Water is a compound made from the elements hydrogen and oxygen.
tf.explanation: Water is a compound because hydrogen and oxygen are chemically combined in a fixed ratio.

tf.questionText: Pure water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius at normal atmospheric pressure.
tf.explanation: The freezing point of pure water is 0 degrees Celsius and its boiling point is 100 degrees Celsius.

tf.questionText: Water can dissolve every known substance, which is why it is called the universal solvent.
tf.explanation: Water dissolves many but not all substances, so 'universal solvent' only means it dissolves a very wide range of materials.

tf.questionText: Hard water lathers easily and quickly with soap.
tf.explanation: Hard water forms scum and lathers poorly because calcium and magnesium ions react with soap.

tf.questionText: Temporary hardness of water can be removed by boiling.
tf.explanation: Boiling decomposes the hydrogencarbonates, removing the temporary hardness.

tf.questionText: Adding washing soda (sodium carbonate) can remove both temporary and permanent hardness.
tf.explanation: Washing soda removes calcium and magnesium ions as insoluble carbonates, softening both types of hard water.

tf.questionText: Blue cobalt chloride paper turns pink when it touches water.
tf.explanation: The colour change from blue to pink is a test used to detect water.

tf.questionText: Hydrogen peroxide and water have exactly the same chemical formula.
tf.explanation: Water is H2O while hydrogen peroxide is H2O2, so they are different compounds.

tf.questionText: Hydrogen peroxide can be used as a bleaching agent for hair and fabrics.
tf.explanation: Its oxidising ability allows hydrogen peroxide to bleach hair, fabrics and other materials.

tf.questionText: Heating water and condensing the steam in distillation produces water with dissolved salts still in it.
tf.explanation: Distillation leaves dissolved salts behind, so the condensed water is very pure.

summary.correctAnswer: Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen with formula H2O.
summary.explanation: Each molecule has two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom.

summary.questionText: Boiling and freezing points of pure water
summary.correctAnswer: Pure water boils at 100 degrees Celsius and freezes at 0 degrees Celsius.
summary.explanation: These fixed points apply at normal atmospheric pressure.

summary.correctAnswer: Water dissolves a very wide range of substances, so it is called the universal solvent.
summary.explanation: This property makes water important in living things and in industry.

summary.correctAnswer: Hardness is caused by dissolved calcium and magnesium salts.
summary.explanation: These ions react with soap to form scum.

summary.correctAnswer: Temporary hardness is removed by boiling; permanent hardness needs washing soda or ion exchange.
summary.explanation: Temporary hardness comes from hydrogencarbonates, permanent from sulphates and chlorides.

summary.correctAnswer: Hardness is removed by boiling, adding washing soda, or using ion-exchange resins.
summary.explanation: These methods remove calcium and magnesium ions.

summary.correctAnswer: Water turns white anhydrous copper(II) sulphate blue and blue cobalt chloride paper pink.
summary.explanation: These colour changes confirm the presence of water.

summary.questionText: Treatment of water for domestic use
summary.correctAnswer: Water is treated by sedimentation, coagulation with alum, filtration, then chlorination.
summary.explanation: These steps remove particles and kill germs to make water safe to drink.

summary.correctAnswer: Hydrogen peroxide decomposes into water and oxygen: 2H2O2 gives 2H2O plus O2.
Hydrogen peroxide is used as an antiseptic, a bleaching agent and a source of oxygen.
summary.explanation: It works because it is an oxidising agent that releases oxygen.

hoq.questionText: A student tests a water sample: it produces poor lather with soap before boiling, and still produces poor lather after boiling. Which conclusion is correct?

options.text: The water has only temporary hardness
The water contains only dissolved chlorine

hoq.explanation: Because boiling did not improve lathering, the hardness is not removed by heat and is therefore permanent hardness.

hoq.questionText: When 2H2O2 fully decomposes to 2H2O and O2, what mass of oxygen gas is produced from 68 g of hydrogen peroxide? (H2O2 = 34, O2 = 32)
hoq.explanation: 68 g of H2O2 is 2 moles, which produce 1 mole of O2; one mole of O2 has a mass of 32 g.

hoq.questionText: Why does adding washing soda soften permanent hard water while boiling alone does not?

options.text: Washing soda raises the temperature higher than boiling
Washing soda removes calcium and magnesium ions as insoluble carbonates
Washing soda adds more calcium ions to the water
Washing soda evaporates the hardness away

hoq.explanation: Permanent hardness comes from sulphates and chlorides that are not broken down by heat, but washing soda precipitates the calcium and magnesium ions as insoluble carbonates.
